findings.title: The obvious one-line implementation was the refuse trigger - flipping `stale` would have caused exactly the refusal the ruling rejected
findings.detail: DRIFT_POLICY defaults to 'refuse' (fail-closed, :129) and synapse_scout raises ScoutError when table_status['stale'] is true (:850-853). Setting stale=True on the external path - the natural reading of 'report the authority as stale' - would have made every CI run, farm node and stock-python process raise instead of ground, which is both the refusal the ruling ruled against and the disarming the brief forbade. In this module stale=True is also structurally coupled to gate-down: both pre-existing sites that set it also set loaded=False and return None. The honest signal therefore needed its own field on its own axis: verified_against_running_build.

findings.title: The token 'stale' is reserved for the corpus-drift axis in the warnings channel - a second, independent reason the report needed a different name
findings.detail: test_fresh_corpus_not_stale asserts `not any('stale' in w.lower() for w in out['warnings'])` for a fresh corpus. Since the new warning fires on every external call, any message containing the word 'stale' would have failed that test. Found by running the suite, not by reasoning - the message is worded around it (prior-major / unverified against a running build).

findings.title: The warning text is deliberately ASCII - an em dash in a warning written to a redirected stderr under a cp1252 locale is a UnicodeEncodeError on exactly the path this change targets
findings.detail: The module's prose uses em dashes freely, but _warn_build_mismatch's warning text does not, and warnings.warn writes through sys.stderr, whose encoding on a Windows farm/CI process with redirected output is the locale codec rather than UTF-8. The first draft used an em dash; it was replaced with '-' before commit. Cost: nothing. Producer: the console mangling visible in the first pytest run of this leg.

findings.title: Observation, not repaired: _WARN accumulates for callers that use _load_symbol_table without going through synapse_scout
findings.detail: _WARN is cleared only at synapse_scout entry, so a process calling _load_symbol_table directly in a loop would accumulate lines. The one such caller in the tree, harness/verify/checks.py:548, calls it once per check invocation, and the next synapse_scout call clears the list. This is a pre-existing module pattern (_check_freshness:713 and the semantic-path helpers at :226/:358/:370 append the same way), NOT introduced here. Deliberately not deduped: a per-result warning is the honest choice, because deduping would make the second scout result silently omit a warning the first one carried.

why: The one-line target was booby-trapped: the single line that would have encoded 'report it as stale' is the DRIFT_POLICY=refuse trigger (WARN-F1). The honest encoding needs its own status field, its own message and a dedupe set.
The module already runs two warn channels at different cadences (result['warnings'] per call, RuntimeWarning once per process); matching that precedent is the dedupe guard.

Law 1 owes a test. A ruled behaviour change shipped unpinned is a decoration - so two tests, each stating its failure condition, one carrying a control that proves the check can fail and simultaneously pins the in-Houdini shape.
estimate_variance.scope_discipline: Per warn.md:21-23 this stopped at the smallest honest diff. Nothing was refactored, no other caller adjusted, no adjacent finding repaired, and WARN-F4 was recorded rather than fixed.

for_ruling.question: Should the in-Houdini path also emit verified_against_running_build=True, for symmetry?
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I - a value judgement between two defensible readings of the brief, not a fact. The brief says 'no behavior change for in-Houdini processes', and adding a key to the status dict IS a change to what an in-Houdini caller sees, so it was NOT added. The cost of that choice: absence-means-verified, which a consumer must know to read with .get(). The alternative is a self-describing status on both paths at the price of a (tiny) in-Houdini change.
for_ruling.shipped_meanwhile: The key appears on the external path only. In-Houdini output is byte-identical to before.

for_ruling.question: Should python/synapse/panel/gate_stamp.py mirror this signal in the panel footer?
for_ruling.why_escalated: Out of the ruled scope (scout only) and structurally unreachable today - gate_stamp returns early unless `import hou` succeeds, so a no-Houdini process never reaches its logic. It is raised because gate_stamp exists precisely to keep panel and tool from disagreeing (its own docstring), and this change makes them disagree about one state the panel can never be in. Cosmetic drift, recorded not worked around.
